title: Telemetry-paused gradient rollback with session borrowing
author: Anika Shah
description: Motivation: reduce noisy immediate rollbacks and enable safer, incremental rollbacks that can pause and resume based on telemetry and human signals. This PR implements a 'telemetry-paused gradient rollback' controller: when a canary produces out-of-bound signals (latency, error rate, semantic drift), the system steps down traffic in configurable gradients but can enter a PAUSED state if secondary signals (user-impact traces, large cohort variance, KV-cache thrash) are ambiguous. A paused rollout exports detailed telemetry and allows 'session borrowing' which temporarily directs a small, controlled set of user sessions to the canary under tight SLO gating for deterministic repro and deeper diagnostics. The design balances automated protection with investigability and minimizes noisy churn by avoiding full immediate reverts for transient anomalies. Checklist: - [x] Implement gradient rollback controller with pause/resume semantics - [x] Add session-borrowing proxy and session-affinity tokens - [x] New SLO gates: latency_delta, error_delta, semantic_kl - [x] Trace/span instrumentation for rollout.state and session.borrow_id - [x] E2E smoke tests + canary repro harness - [x] Documentation + runbook updates Linked work: ENG-4821, ENG-4902 (investigation), PM-1147 (product gating). Related: SUP-1298 (customer incident where immediate reverts made debugging impossible). Summary of behavior: when metric thresholds breach, controller computes a per-step traffic decrement schedule (default 20% steps). After each step it waits for a sampling window; if signals stay ambiguous the controller transitions to PAUSED and emits an investigative bundle: recent traces, cohort-level diffs, and a snapshot of prefix/KV cache. Operators can then choose to resume gradient rollback, continue paused (extend window), or commit a full revert. Session borrowing: operators may enable session borrowing which pins a tiny cohort (default 0.05% of sessions) to the canary with session tokens; this cohort is routed with strict timeout and enhanced tracing to help reproduce SLO regressions without worsening global impact. Safety: - canary rollback cannot drive stable below min_capacity threshold - session borrowing is bounded by token quota and circuit-breaker - all paused transitions are auditable via rollout.audit entries and trace attributes Implementation notes: controller changes (controller/rollout_manager.go) add state machine (NORMAL -> GRADIENT_ROLLBACK -> PAUSED -> RESUME/REVERT), new APIs (POST /rollouts/:id/pause, /resume), and a compact telemetry bundle producer. Proxy changes (proxy/session_borrow.go) implement token issuance and affinity. Observability: new metrics rollout_pause_count, session_borrow_active, rollout_step_duration_seconds, semantic_kl_score; new tracing tags rollout.state and session.borrow_id. Backwards compatibility: preserves existing canary configs; new fields opt-in via rollout.policy.pause_on_ambiguous_signals. Migration: rollout configs will be accepted by old controllers (ignored fields) but only new controllers respond to pause/resume. See release notes below for config hints.

release_notes: - Introduces telemetry-paused gradient rollback: safer automated rollback with pause/resume for ambiguous signals. - Adds session borrowing to repro regressions with minimal global impact. - New metrics: rollout_pause_count, session_borrow_active, rollout_step_duration_seconds, semantic_kl_score. - New API endpoints: POST /rollouts/:id/pause and /rollouts/:id/resume. Operators must opt-in via rollout.policy.pause_on_ambiguous_signals.
notes_for_ops: Operators: default rollout behavior unchanged. To use pause/resume and session borrowing, add 'pause_on_ambiguous_signals: true' to your rollout.policy. Session borrowing defaults: cohort 0.05%, token_ttl 30m, token_quota 500. If you see frequent PAUSED states review semantic_kl_score and cohort variance metrics; use the runbook docs/runbooks/rollout_pause_and_investigation.md for guided debugging.
risk_assessment: medium (new state transitions and a small proxy surface area). Mitigations: opt-in policy, bounded session borrowing, circuit-breakers, and extensive e2e smoke coverage.
